text:
jia: Heads-up — during the Canary deploy we saw observability ingest spike ~8x for ~6m and caused indexing lag and huge bill. We should design an adaptive shedder that protects downstream storage while preserving cost attribution fidelity.

sam: Agreed. Quick Q: is this sampling (keep subset) or shedding (drop)? They have different recovery/analysis implications. :thinking:

maria: We probably need a hybrid. For billing/chargeback we must keep at least 1 exemplar per tenant per minute (or an org-minimum) so cost attribution stays readable. Dropping everything for a tenant will break billing.

leo: Proposal sketch: per-tenant reservoir sampling + guaranteed exemplars per billing tier + emergency hard-shed for global overload windows. We can fast-path decisions based on three cheap signals: recent token count, unique-span-cardinality, and billing-tier. Pseudoconfig: 
```yaml
policy:
  window_secs: 60
  global_max_events_per_sec: 12000
  exemplar_guarantee: {enterprise: 10, standard: 2, free: 1}
  tenant_shed_watermark: 0.7    # start shedding when tenant uses 70% of allocated window budget
  emergency_shed_fraction: 0.25 # fraction to drop globally under overload
```

sam: Need to be explicit about labels we attach so analytics and evals can reweight. If we reservoir-sample we should emit metadata like `sample_kind=reservoir, seed=1234, exemplar=true/false`. If shed, emit `dropped=quota|overload`. That way downstream can compensate.

jia: Exactly. Also handshake: ingestion should accept a `billing_key` header and keep it at the envelope root so late enrichment won't lose tenant mapping. If billing_key is missing, fall back to tenant-id but mark as `billing_inferred=true`.

maria: Another constraint: tracing/parent-child integrity. We must not drop spans that cause entire trace to look like it originated from an unrelated service. Keep root span exemplars preferentially.

ingest-bot: ALERT: ingest_queue_delay > 300ms for 4m (prod-ingest-1). See runbook: https://go/runbooks/ingest-backpressure

sam: For rollout: implement feature-flagged shedder in front of hot path, run in dry-run for 24h with `dropped` flags only, check cost delta + fidelity metrics. Metrics to capture: `obs.shed_rate`, `obs.shed_by_reason{quota,overload}`, `obs.exemplars_retained_per_tenant`, and `obs.shed_latency_added_ms`.

leo: Also add a debug endpoint to retrieve per-tenant window state (read-only) and a sampled stream of dropped envelopes for manual inspection (consent-only).

jia: Action items: (1) leo to draft RFC + config prototype by EOD Thursday, (2) sam to add telemetry panels and alert thresholds, (3) maria to enumerate billing-tier exemplar requirements and backward-compat checks, (4) eng-sre to update runbook after dry-run.

leo: I'll put the RFC up at /rfc/ingest-adaptive-shedder by EOD Thu. Will include perf sims and a small k6 script. :thumbsup:

maria: One more: ensure we don't mutate or remove billing keys during late enrichment. If any team is currently dropping billing info in enrichment, we need a migration plan.

sam: Noted. I'll add an integration test that synthesizes missing billing_key and asserts `billing_inferred` label is present.

jia: Thanks everyone. If you want to collaborate on the RFC comments, ping me or add inline. cc @eng-sre for immediate runbook follow-up.
